clue.text: Singer can be made to give up

indicators.note: the letters of the word before can be made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist can be forced to quit performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' tells you to rework the six letters of SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a post or abandon a contest is to relinquish it, the same as to give it up.

clue.text: Paid for redemption, part in African money

indicators.note: the word for part goes inside the South African currency

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Bought back, partly in South African currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive freed on payment has been redeemed by money handed over.

clue.text: Noticed clean, fine wood

parts.note: saw means noticed
to dust is to clean

explanation.surface: Spotted some clean, high-quality timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like praise of the wood, but it means powdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny particles of wood are produced when timber is cut.

clue.text: Moving target a V1 will sink

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about

parts.note: V1 read as the letters V and I

explanation.surface: A flying bomb will bring down a target on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges TARGET, A and VI (the V1 flying bomb with its 1 read as I).
explanation.definitionFit: To be drawn down by the pull of weight is to settle or descend.

clue.text: Great admirer (self-proclaimed) of procrastination

parts.note: someone proclaiming about themselves says I
the motto of a procrastinator is 'do later'

explanation.surface: A self-confessed big fan of putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The procrastinator's own words, 'I do later', run together to spell someone who worships.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships an idol is, by extension, an excessive devotee of anything.

clue.text: Two girls I sum up thus?

parts.note: Dot and Carry (Carrie) are two girls' names
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pair of girls doing their arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The old schoolroom phrase for adding columns: write the units digit and carry the tens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase recites the steps of column addition, writing a digit and carrying the remainder.

clue.text: Left that second European city

parts.note: yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Someone departed from that other continental town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyons is the English spelling of Lyon, a major city in France.

clue.text: In that neither will change

indicators.note: the letters of the word before will change their order

explanation.surface: In that case, nobody will change.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word for 'in that place or matter'.

clue.text: Go round, right, getting up to mischief in person

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief, mischief personified

explanation.surface: Someone up to no good does a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns TO into OT; Ate, the Greek goddess of rash mischief, is mischief personified.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve or turn about an axis is to spin.

clue.text: Cut a fine figure perhaps in a dangerous situation

definitions.meaning: trace a figure while skating on a delicate surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut a fine figure' looks like the idiom for looking good, but it is a figure-skater's figure cut on thin ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater on a fragile surface is literally taking a risk, the idiom for courting danger.

clue.text: Town where bets are on the cards

definitions.meaning: a Suffolk town, the headquarters of British horse racing

definitions.text: where bets are on the cards
definitions.meaning: a card game in which players stake money on certain cards

explanation.surface: A place where wagering is likely to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' looks like the idiom for 'likely', but it is literal: the card game Newmarket has stakes placed on cards. The Suffolk town is Britain's horse-racing centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The racing town and the gambling card game share one name.

clue.text: Public deliveries before beginning of term

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by the bowler

indicators.note: the beginning of the word term is its first letter

explanation.surface: Communal handouts before school starts back.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a cricket term: six balls bowled in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and not concealed is done in plain view, in public.

clue.text: O, Copper, hearken, and 1'll help you set

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to list is an old word for to listen

explanation.surface: An appeal to a policeman to listen, with a promise of help in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol CU. LIST as 'listen' is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist, the speaker of the definition, assists people's vision.

clue.text: Coming back, an aroma

indicators.note: 'coming back' makes the little word an run backwards

parts.note: an aroma is a scent

explanation.surface: A smell returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' looks like one phrase, but 'Coming' is the definition and 'back' turns AN into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just emerging is beginning to exist, about to arrive in the sense of coming into being.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.definitionFit: A bye or wide is a bonus run in cricket, and anything left over is surplus.

clue.text: He's in love with many a prize worker

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a cup is a trophy
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A man smitten with lots of trophy-winning labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is C, a hundred in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is the person who is inside a house or seat.

clue.text: One Caledonian goes up in flames before an Andorran perhaps for a spell

indicators.note: the first part comes before the next word
the Scots word goes inside the burning heap

parts.note: a pyre is a heap set in flames

indicators.note: in a down clue goes up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: ane is Scots for one

explanation.surface: A Scot is burnt on a pyre ahead of a visitor from Andorra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' reverses the Scots word in this down clue. 'Caledonian' is a poetic word for Scottish; 'for a spell' makes the definition a temporary resident of the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra lies in the mountains between France and Spain, so someone there is a mountain dweller of that range.

clue.text: Continues to claim and press it's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Keeps asserting and pushing that it's odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PRESS and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere in an assertion is to keep maintaining it.

clue.text: Highlight "Yellow Bird'

parts.note: to accent something is to emphasise it
or is the heraldic gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Emphasise the title of a song about a yellow bird.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold, i.e. yellow, in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow or dunnock belongs to the accentor family of songbirds.

clue.text: In which a soldier was over six feet?

definitions.text: In which a soldier was over six feet?

parts.words: In which a soldier was over six feet?
parts.note: a mounted soldier sat above the six feet: his two and his horse's four

explanation.walkthrough: 'over six feet' looks like height, but counts the rider's two feet and his horse's four.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted troops each had a horse under them, six feet in all.

clue.text: Ransack what's left in common

indicators.note: the letter for left sits inside the word for common

parts.note: rife means widespread

explanation.surface: Plunder whatever remains in shared land.
explanation.definitionFit: To search a place thoroughly and rob it is to plunder or loot it.

clue.text: Licence fee's about right, do get married

indicators.note: the word for fee goes about the letter for right

parts.note: taken as the word fee
taken as written

explanation.surface: The cost of a permit is about right, so go ahead and wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence here is liberty, the absence of restriction.

clue.text: Where Poles found a bird without a bill

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside

parts.note: a crow is a bird
an account, abbreviated AC, is a bill

explanation.surface: Poles discovered a bird with no beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but means 'outside'. Cracow (Kraków) is a Polish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracow is a historic city of southern Poland.

clue.text: Food for Italian rebel leader a fiddle? Not quite

indicators.note: the leader of the word rebel is its opening letter
the instrument falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Something to eat for an Italian insurgent chief who plays the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the last letter from VIOLIN, leaving VIOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta parcels stuffed with meat or cheese are a classic dish of Italy.

clue.text: The conclusion in some game

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters

explanation.surface: The final result of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end.

clue.text: In turn try to get a vote against the Americans

indicators.note: in turn means the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: to seek is to try to get
a nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: Each in turn attempts to win a no vote against the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' reverses SEEK + NAY together to give YAN + KEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is a familiar name for people from the United States.

clue.text: Produce young tyro in place of Adullam

indicators.note: the learner letter sits inside the biblical hiding place

parts.note: in the Bible David hid in the cave of Adullam
a tyro is a learner, L as on learner plates

explanation.surface: A novice gives birth in a biblical hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: The cave of Adullam is where David hid from Saul (1 Samuel 22).
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and whales bear offspring, giving birth to a calf.

clue.text: Insinuations end unions' disruption

indicators.note: disruption throws the letters of the two words into disorder

explanation.surface: Disruption brings unions to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' rearranges END and UNIONS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly hints and veiled suggestions are oblique remarks implying something.

clue.text: Sounds from a stray country traveller

indicators.note: sounds says the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a waif is a stray, and an area is a country or region

explanation.surface: Noises made by a wandering rural type.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WAIF AREA runs together into a word for a traveller on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying, especially on foot.

clue.text: Hostility from bird who's turned against us

indicators.note: the bird's name is turned round

parts.note: mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Ill will from a bird that has turned on us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's turned' reverses MINA to ANIM; 'against' just sets it beside US.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity or ill feeling is enmity directed at someone.
